newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius cuts 1996 sugar crop to 590,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius cuts 1996 sugar crop to 590,000 T.

text.p: Mauritian sugar authorities on Monday revised their 1996 sugar production forecast downwards again, to 590,000 tonnes from a May forecast of 610,000 tonnes.

The Public Relations Office of the Sugar Industry (Prosi) said, "On the basis of data available as at 25 November 1996, the (Mauritius) Chamber of Agriculture feels that sugar production 1996 will be at 590,000 tonnes, around 3.0 percent less than an initial forecast of 610,000 tonnes made before the start of the sugar cane harvest."
The government earlier gave a preliminary 1996 production forecast of 625,000 tonnes. The Chamber of Agriculture then scaled that down to 610,000 tonnes.
Mauritius produced 539,521 tonnes of sugar in 1995.
In a statement, Prosi blamed the poorer production on drought in Mauritius since last August and an initial underestimation of the impact of a cyclone in February.

"With two sugar mills still in operation as at 25 November, it looks like the severe drought affecting the country at the moment and which has lasted since August 1996, had negative repercussions at the end of the harvest on cane production at low altitude and production near the coast," Prosi added.
Prosi also said this contributed in lowering the cane yield (per hectare of land under cultivation) during these past weeks but did not give sugar cane yield figures.

"Moreover, it appears clearly today that (cyclone) Edwige, with cyclonic winds of more than 120 km per hour....had a negative impact more important than initially anticipated on cane cultivation in certain regions," Prosi said.
It added that cane yields in the island's central and southern regions were negatively affected by cyclone Edwige.
